summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Novos Power is the fourth and by far the smallest name in SemiAnalysis's May 2026 solid-state-transformer vendor set — a 2025 San Diego university spin-out (SDSU Distinguished Professor Chris Mi as co-founder and CTO, Stanford GSB graduate Susan Linwood as co-founder and CEO) with a 2–10-person team, a four-page template website whose blog is empty, no disclosed funding round, no SEC Form D, no patent or paper on its technology visible in any public database, no named customer, and no product on the record beyond a name — the Variable Airgap Solid State Transformer (VASST) — and a set of company-stated figures (direct 13–48 kV utility input, ≥98.5% peak efficiency, 1–50 MW, DC 400–1,500 V, air cooling, response '1000x faster than the current setup'). As of 19 September 2026 its public record consists of two pitch-competition wins (FedTech's Crucible Ignitor studio, February 2026; UC San Diego's Golden Ticket to the Horizon Accelerator, June 2026), a showcase slot at the IEEE Hard Tech Venture Summit (April 2026), the CTO's academic talks describing 'a novel megawatt-scale, medium-voltage power conversion system based on a Variable Air Gap Solid-State Transformer architecture', platinum sponsorship of SDSU's AI x Energy Summit, and one analyst citation. BACKGROUND. Novos Power Inc. is a Delaware corporation registered in California on 7 November 2025 (state-record mirror); the concept predates the entity — LACI's June 2025 cohort blurb for ChargePodX, Linwood's earlier company, already describes 'power electronics that convert medium-voltage AC directly into DC, eliminating the need for bulky traditional transformers' for EV charging, data centers and renewables. The company's own description: it 'stabilizes megawatt, millisecond AI load fluctuations', 'connects directly to 13 - 48KV utility feeds, bypassing legacy 480V step-down transformers', and rests on 'decades of DOE and NASA-funded research, with a foundation spanning 300+ peer-reviewed publications and 30+ issued patents'. On the public record that lineage is the CTO's general portfolio — the DOE GATE Center for Electric Drive Transportation he directs, a NASA University Leadership Initiative eVTOL design-tools grant on which he is a team member, and California Energy Commission battery grants — none of which is a solid-state-transformer project; his published patents are in wireless power transfer and battery management. SemiAnalysis (26 May 2026) records that 'Novos Power reports peak efficiencies over 98%', 'is concentrating on direct MV-input units that collapse the LV transformer and rectifier into a single device' and 'uses air cooling through proprietary insulation', and thanks the company in its acknowledgments; a secondary summary of the same piece adds 'claiming a 50% footprint reduction'. The company itself says it has 'not just one product, but a rich architecture roadmap' — a '5 generations technical roadmap' with no dates. Collection gap: no datasheet, topology, cell count, switching frequency, unit rating, test result, delivery date, price, customer, pilot, investor or round exists in any source; sec.gov is blocked from this environment but efts.sec.gov full-text search returns no Form D; the Delaware record, the Google and Silicon Valley AI Summit awards and the LACI incubation claim could not be verified from any organiser page (LACI's three 2025–2026 cohort lists carry ChargePodX, not Novos Power).
ecosystemRole: We assess Novos Power as a pre-product entrant in the hall-edge power-conversion layer — a claimed direct medium-voltage (13–48 kV) to DC solid-state transformer that would compete with Heron Link, Amperesand's platform and DG Matrix's roadmap Cell-MV for the 34.5 kV-to-800 V DC block, and with the hedged incumbents (ABB, Eaton, GE Vernova, Hitachi Energy, Siemens, Schneider Electric) that sit on NVIDIA's facility-tier roster. It has no shipped unit, no listed product and no disclosed capital, and its stated applications (AI data centers, EV fast charging, microgrids, energy storage, on-site generation, defense installations) are the same list every multi-market SST startup carries before it has a customer. It is not a battery, switchgear, UPS or rack power-shelf vendor, and it is absent from every NVIDIA-published 800 VDC list.

productsAndServices.name: Variable Airgap Solid State Transformer (VASST) — medium-voltage solid-state transformer platform (pre-product)
productsAndServices.description: The company's only named product, and it exists on the record as claims rather than as a unit. The site: 'Novos Power connects directly to 13 - 48KV utility feeds, bypassing legacy 480V step-down transformers. Our Variable Airgap Solid State Transformer (VASST) redefines SST -- delivering scalable, high-density power with dynamic responsiveness to millisecond-level GPU load swings'; 'We use high-frequency SiC to maintain voltage stability and prevent GPU restarts. 1000x faster than the current setup'; 'Built with high redundancy and hot-swap capability'; 'Over the lifetime, we reduce power waste by 25% and achieve 50% cost savings between CapEx and OpEx'; 'Our on-board AI transforms reactive power management into proactive power management'. The April 2026 IEEE showcase post: 'VASST (Variable Airgap Solid-State Transformer) replaces 100-year-old copper-and-iron transformer technology with advanced SiC semiconductor-based architecture', 'Built for AI data centers, EV fast charging, microgrids, energy storage, and on-site generation: ≥98.5% peak efficiency; 1–50 MW power ratings; DC 400–1500 V operating range; Real-time smart control + modular grid integration'. The LinkedIn tagline: 'AI-driven, modular power conversion systems that replace legacy transformers, scalable up to 10 MW'. The July 2026 post: 'Novos Power's SST goes directly from the 35 kV line to the GPU — we power the AI racks.' The CTO's May 2026 seminar abstract: 'a novel megawatt-scale, medium-voltage (MV) power conversion system based on a Variable Air Gap Solid-State Transformer architecture' aiming 'to reduce energy loss, footprint, and cost while enabling flexible, modular deployment'. SemiAnalysis (May 2026): 'Novos Power reports peak efficiencies over 98%'; 'concentrating on direct MV-input units that collapse the LV transformer and rectifier into a single device'; 'air cooling through proprietary insulation'. FedTech (February 2026) positions the same unit for defense: 'Their Variable Airgap Solid-State Transformer (VASST) system enables modular, rapid deployment at bases to deliver real-time voltage and frequency regulation during grid stress.' No datasheet, drawing, photograph of hardware, topology description, cell count, switching frequency, cooling specification, weight, footprint figure, certification target or delivery date has been published by the company or reported by anyone else.
highlights: Direct medium-voltage input is the positioning that separates it from DG Matrix (whose shipping unit connects at 480 V) and aligns it with Heron Power and Amperesand — but the input range is stated three ways on the company's own channels ('13 - 48KV', 'the 35 kV line', and 'up to 10 MW' against '1–50 MW' for scale), and 48 kV lies above the 38 kV ceiling of UL 2877, the safety standard that would govern a medium-voltage power supply (UL's scope statement).

'Variable airgap' is the company's stated differentiator and it is undefined on the record: no company document, patent, application, paper or talk abstract explains what is varied, how, or why. Google Patents shows no filing assigned to Novos Power and none by the CTO on a solid-state or air-gap transformer as of 19 September 2026 (a 2025 filing would not publish before 2027).

Every performance figure is a company statement without a unit behind it: '≥98.5% peak efficiency' (company post), 'over 98%' (SemiAnalysis, reporting the company), '1000x faster', '25%' waste reduction and '50%' cost savings (site, no baseline defined), '50% footprint reduction' (a secondary summary of SemiAnalysis). The CTO's own July 2026 scoreboard is of him, not the product: '25 years in power electronics · 30 patents filed · 400 papers · h-index 47'.

Air cooling 'through proprietary insulation' (SemiAnalysis) would be a genuine difference from DG Matrix's liquid-cooled Interport and from the liquid-cooled cell stacks Heron and Amperesand describe, if it exists at medium voltage and megawatt scale — insulation coordination at 13–48 kV in air is the hard problem the claim names without solving on the record (analysis).
The only commercial offer on the record is the site's 'Join our early access program'; no customer, pilot, letter of intent, utility or hyperscaler engagement, price or lead time has been published.
productsAndServices.positioning: Fourth of the four SST startups SemiAnalysis names (with DG Matrix, Heron Power and Amperesand), and the only one with no funding round, no factory, no datasheet and no roster placement. Against Heron Link (4.2 MW, 34.5 kV, on NVIDIA's October 2025 list) and Amperesand (3.3 kV SiC platform, USD 80M Series A, Reno line) it claims the same direct MV-to-DC block with air rather than liquid cooling; against DG Matrix it claims medium-voltage input where DG Matrix ships low-voltage. Against the incumbents (ABB, Eaton, GE Vernova, Hitachi Energy, Siemens, Schneider Electric, Mitsubishi Electric) it has no product to position. Its stated non-data-center markets — EV fast charging, microgrids, storage, on-site generation and, through FedTech, defense installations — mirror the multi-market pitch Amperesand (port charging) and DG Matrix (EV charging, behind-the-meter) each started with.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Not disclosed. The site offers an 'early access program'; FedTech's studio offers 'visibility among Department of War (DoW) prime contractors and private-sector investors' and 'funding connections'. No channel, integrator, EPC or OEM partner is named.

No prototype, pilot, certification or delivery date has been announced.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Novos Power is pre-product and pre-funding. Basis: no datasheet, drawing or hardware photograph on any channel; no customer, pilot or letter of intent; no Form D (efts.sec.gov full-text search, 0 hits for the name in 2025–2026) and no round reported by any outlet; CB Insights' stage 'Biz Plan Competition'; a four-page Wix site last modified 20 March 2026 with placeholder copy ('© 2035', '123-456-7890') and an empty blog; LinkedIn '2-10 employees'. The two non-cash awards and the IEEE showcase are the whole of the external record.

(High confidence) We assess that the 'DOE- and NASA-funded' lineage describes the CTO's research portfolio, not a solid-state-transformer program. Basis: SDSU pages list the DOE GATE Center (electric-drive transportation), a NASA University Leadership Initiative eVTOL design-tools grant led by UC San Diego, and CEC battery grants; Google Patents and FreePatentsOnline return no transformer, air-gap or medium-voltage filing by him (his patents are wireless power transfer and battery management) and none assigned to Novos Power. The '300+ publications / 30+ patents' figure is his career total.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the VASST is the ChargePodX product re-pointed from EV charging to AI data centers — the pivot DG Matrix made a year earlier. Basis: LACI's June 2025 blurb for ChargePodX (Linwood, CEO) already describes medium-voltage-AC-to-DC SiC power electronics 'eliminating the need for bulky traditional transformers'; the Novos site lists EV fast charging among its applications; the company's own 'incubated by LACI' claim matches ChargePodX's cohort, not a Novos Power one.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that 'variable airgap' most plausibly denotes an adjustable inductance in the converter's medium-frequency isolation transformer — an air gap sets a core's magnetizing and leakage inductance, and in a dual-active-bridge cell the series inductance sets how much power a given phase shift transfers, so varying it is one way to hold soft switching and control authority across the light-to-full load swings a GPU cluster produces. This is analysis: the company has disclosed no topology, and no patent, application, paper or talk abstract describes the mechanism. The CTO's published expertise in loosely coupled wireless-power coils — the extreme air-gap case — is consistent with the reading and does not confirm it.

(High confidence) We assess that Novos Power is absent from every NVIDIA-published 800 VDC list and from every 2026 SST roundup except SemiAnalysis. Basis: NVIDIA's May 2025 and October 2025 developer blogs and its August 2026 corporate post name no Novos Power; Power Electronics News' GTC 2026 list and its May 2026 'real-world SSTs' piece (which names Heron, DG Matrix, SolarEdge, Amperesand, Hyperscale Power and Enphase) omit it; so do TechCrunch (February and March 2026), Heatmap (April 2026), mgrid and Bessemer. SemiAnalysis's acknowledgments show the company briefed that piece.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the near-term commercial path runs through accelerators, pitch competitions and defense installations rather than hyperscalers. Basis: FedTech's studio pitches VASST for 'defense installations' and 'bases'; the Golden Ticket delivers accelerator residency; the Generator Reliability Summit audience is the backup-power community; the only offer on the site is an 'early access program'. At the pace of the three funded siblings — USD 60–140M raised each, factories announced, and still no listed medium-voltage unit — a 2–10-person team without a round is several years from a certified 13–48 kV product; the '5 generations' roadmap has no dates because the first generation has none.

(Low confidence) We assess that the 48 kV upper bound is a marketing envelope rather than a design point: 46 kV is a subtransmission class above the 15/25/35 kV distribution classes at which US data centers are served, and UL 2877's scope stops at 38 kV, so a 48 kV-input unit would fall outside the medium-voltage power-supply standard as written. The later '35 kV line' wording is the plausible design target. No source states either.

INDICATORS TO WATCH — through Q2 2027: a priced round or Form D (converts Judgment 1); any published patent application naming Novos Power or a variable-air-gap transformer (tests Judgment 4 and dates the IP); a datasheet, prototype photograph, unit rating or test result from the Horizon Accelerator residency or an SDSU/UCSD demonstration (the first hardware evidence); a named pilot — defense base, microgrid, charging depot or data hall — from either party (tests Judgment 6); appearance on any NVIDIA page, OCP contributor list or trade-press SST roundup beyond SemiAnalysis (tests Judgment 5); a UL 2877 or UL 1741 target date; and the CEO's or CTO's departure from ChargePodX or SDSU roles, which would signal the company has become full-time.

policyExposure.regime: UL 2877 / UL 1741 / IEEE 1547 certification for medium-voltage power-conversion equipment
policyExposure.exposure: No company document names a safety standard, a certification target date or a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory. UL 2877's scope statement — 'power supplies having ac or dc input voltage ratings above 1000 V, up to 38 kV, and ac or dc output voltage ratings up to 38 kV' — would govern a 13–35 kV-input unit; the site's 48 kV upper bound lies above that ceiling. Grid-interactive behaviour at the point of common coupling would be tested to IEEE 1547 through the UL 1741 supplements. The three funded SST siblings each name their targets and none had completed a data-center SST listing as of May 2026 (Power Electronics News).

policyExposure.regime: Federal defense-innovation commercialisation channel (FedTech Crucible / Department of War prime contractors)
policyExposure.exposure: FedTech's release states that its Crucible winners gain 'visibility among Department of War (DoW) prime contractors and private-sector investors' and 'the exposure, guidance, and funding connections they need', and its own page pitches VASST for 'defense installations' and 'bases' — 'real-time voltage and frequency regulation during grid stress'. The Ignitor studio 'is dedicated to emerging, early-stage concepts with high market potential'; no contract, award value or program of record is stated.
policyExposure.mitigation: None stated by the company beyond the award itself.

metrics.result: Company statement versus public record: the lineage is real but not transformer-specific

periods.commentary: Private, pre-revenue and pre-round on every public source. Nothing a buyer or investor would price on — unit cost, measured efficiency, a prototype rating, a pilot, headcount beyond '2-10' — is disclosed. The dossier records the awards as their organisers describe them and the company's own claims as claims.

financials.commentary: There is no financial record to assess. The comparison that matters is with the three funded SST siblings: Heron Power (USD 140M Series B, Morgan Hill factory), Amperesand (USD 80M Series A, Reno line) and DG Matrix (USD 60M Series A, Morrisville plant) each raised institutional capital before publishing a datasheet, and none has a listed medium-voltage unit; Novos Power has raised nothing on the record and has published less. Expected fields are empty because no benchmark exists.
